name: OSINT — Event Chronology
description: Build a defensible event graph where time claims carry provenance and uncertainty instead of being flattened into one neat fiction.

tasks.name: Collect and preserve evidence
tasks.objective: Collect relevant public records, posts, media, reports, sensor/transport/weather data, archives, and supplied evidence. Preserve originals, retrieval times, platform identifiers, and deletions/edits where observable.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Evidence items have stable IDs and provenance before timeline synthesis.

tasks.name: Normalize temporal claims
tasks.objective: Extract source timestamps, embedded metadata, quoted event times, inferred times, time zones, clock uncertainty, upload delays, daylight-saving effects, and platform timestamp semantics. Convert only after preserving originals.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Original and normalized times are both retained with conversion rules.

tasks.name: Build event dependency graph
tasks.objective: Represent events and evidence as a graph with before/after, causes, observations, communications, movements, and shared references. Keep contradictory versions as separate hypotheses rather than overwriting them.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every event node identifies the evidence supporting its time/order.

tasks.name: Constrain uncertain times
tasks.objective: Use shadows/sun, weather, traffic, scheduled broadcasts, transport traces, construction state, illumination, callouts in media, archive captures, and other contextual anchors to narrow uncertain capture/event windows.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Inferred windows state assumptions and cannot masquerade as source timestamps.

tasks.name: Resolve or preserve conflicts
tasks.objective: Test conflicts for clock error, repost delay, time-zone mistakes, edited media, misidentified event, duplicate event, or source unreliability. Resolve only when evidence discriminates; otherwise preserve competing timelines.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Unresolved contradictions remain visible in the final chronology.

tasks.name: Publish chronology with confidence
tasks.objective: Produce a human-readable and machine-readable timeline/event graph distinguishing confirmed times, bounded windows, relative order, source claims, and unknowns; include evidence links, provenance, assumptions, and key gaps.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Readers can see why each event is placed where it is and how certain that placement is.
